title: Best ways to make contactless payments while travelling
summary: Discover the best ways to make contactless payments while travelling. Use Apple Pay, Google Pay and international cards for smooth payments abroad.
body_markdown:
When you are travelling, small moments move fast.


You land in a new country. You need a taxi. You grab a coffee while figuring out directions. You pay for metro tickets, museum entries, and last-minute train rides. Nobody wants to stand at the counter counting notes or worrying whether their card will be accepted.


Contactless payments have become one of the easiest ways to move through a new place without friction. But not all contactless methods work equally well abroad.


Here are the best ways to make contactless payments while travelling and how to choose the right setup.


## 1. Use Apple Pay or Google Pay for tap-and-go payments


One of the most reliable ways to make contactless payments while travelling is through[Apple Pay](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-use-apple-pay-worldwide-with-your-grey-card) or[Google Pay](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-use-google-pay-worldwide-with-your-grey-virtual-card) .


Instead of pulling out your physical card, you tap your phone or smartwatch on the terminal. Your card details stay encrypted, and merchants never see the full number.


**Why it works well abroad:**


- Accepted in most countries that support contactless
- Faster than chip-and-PIN
- Adds an extra layer of security
- Reduces the risk of card skimming


If you lose your phone, you can remotely disable payments. That is much harder to do with cash.

## 2. Use a card built for international spending


Many travellers discover that their domestic debit card works perfectly at home but struggles abroad. Some are blocked automatically. Others add high foreign transaction fees.


The best way to make contactless payments while travelling is to use a card designed for international use.


The[Grey virtual card](https://grey.co/cards) , for example, connects directly to your foreign currency balances and works seamlessly with[Apple Pay and Google Pay](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-add-your-grey-card-to-apple-pay-or-google-pay) . That means you can tap your phone in cafés, shops, transport terminals and hotels without manually topping up or switching accounts before every purchase.


Because it is built for cross-border spending, there are fewer unexpected declines compared to local-only cards.


**You may also like:**[How to pay online and in stores worldwide with your phone](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-pay-online-and-in-stores-worldwide-with-your-phone)


## 3. Avoid relying only on cash


Cash feels safe, but it creates its own problems:


- You need to exchange money at airports
- You may get unfavourable rates
- You risk carrying large amounts
- You cannot easily track spending


Contactless payments give you a digital trail. You can see every transaction instantly inside your app. This is especially useful when travelling across multiple cities or countries.


## 4. Enable 3D Secure and payment alerts


Security matters even more when travelling.


Public Wi-Fi, unfamiliar networks and tourist-heavy areas increase exposure to fraud.


Before your trip:


- Activate transaction notifications
- Enable 3D Secure authentication
- Set daily spending limits


The[Grey virtual card](https://grey.co/cards) supports 3D Secure and integrates with Apple Pay and Google Pay, which add biometric verification such as fingerprint or Face ID. That means even if someone gets access to your device, they cannot easily complete a payment.

## 5. Use contactless for transport and quick purchases


Many cities now allow direct tap-to-pay access on:


- Metro systems
- Buses
- Airport trains
- Trams


Instead of buying physical tickets, you can tap your phone at the gate. It saves time and avoids queues.


Contactless is also ideal for:


- Coffee shops
- Convenience stores
- Food markets
- Ride-hailing services


When you are moving constantly, speed matters.


## Why contactless payments are the smartest option for modern travellers


Travelling today is digital.


Boarding passes live in your phone. Hotel confirmations arrive by email. Navigation happens through apps. Payments should match that flow.


The best ways to make contactless payments while travelling combine:


- Internationally accepted cards
- Mobile wallet integration
- Strong security features
- Clear visibility over transactions


With the Grey virtual card connected to Apple Pay or Google Pay, you can pay quickly, securely and internationally without constantly worrying about currency conversions or blocked transactions.


If you are planning your next trip, setting up the right payment method before you leave can make the entire experience smoother.
